---
title: "Read the automatic checks on GitHub"
subtitle: "SOP SYS-05 · Technical systems manual"
---

## Purpose

Read the results of the checks GitHub runs on every change, and decide
whether a change is safe to merge.

## Applies to

The person responsible for the shop's database, before merging any pull
request.

## Before you begin

- You can sign in to the project on GitHub:
  [github.com/jasonrwilliams-maker/dog-groomer-platform](https://github.com/jasonrwilliams-maker/dog-groomer-platform).

## What GitHub checks

Every time a change is pushed, and on every pull request, GitHub builds the
project from scratch on its own computers and runs four checks. They use only
the made-up test dogs. They never see real paperwork or the AI's API key.

| Check | What it proves |
|---|---|
| **pgTAP suite** | Every database rule still refuses what it should. The same tests as [SYS-04](database-tests.qmd) |
| **Groomer API tests** | The shop screens' connection to the database still works |
| **Groomer interface type-check and build** | The shop's screens still build without errors |
| **Extraction harness self-check** | The scoring of the AI's readings is still correct |

The project's front page on GitHub shows a **tests** badge at the top of the
README. **passing** in green means the latest checks on `master` passed.

## Procedure

1. Open the pull request on GitHub.
2. Scroll down to the box above the **Merge pull request** button. It shows
   the checks:
   - **All checks have passed**, with a green check mark: go to step 5.
   - A yellow dot: the checks are still running. Wait a few minutes and
     reload the page.
   - **Some checks were not successful**, with a red ✕: go to step 3.
3. Click **Details** beside the check with the red ✕. The check's log opens.
   The step that failed is marked with a red ✕. Click it to read its output.
4. Do not merge. Fix the problem on the same branch and push again. The
   checks run again by themselves.

   If the failure looks unrelated to the change, for example a download that
   timed out, click **Re-run jobs** at the top right of the log, then
   **Re-run failed jobs**.

5. Merge the pull request.

### See every run

The **Actions** tab at the top of the project on GitHub lists every run.
Runs named **tests** are these checks. Runs named **browser demo** publish
the demo and the manual; see [SYS-06](publishing.qmd).

## Result

The pull request shows **All checks have passed** before it is merged, and the
**tests** badge on the README says **passing**.
